hook.line: What happens when you ask ChatGPT to erase your whole digital footprint? I tried it.
hook.visual: Creator close-up in a warm room talking straight to camera, white pill title 'ChatGPT erased my digital identity' with an emoji above his head, single-word caption at chest height.

beats.what: Face-to-camera question plus the claim that it actually worked, title pill on screen.
Hard cut to the payoff first: a checklist of data-broker sites, each with a green tick and 'removal request in process'.
Screen recording of the ChatGPT box as prompt 1 is typed in, voice reads it aloud.
Table of broker sites with opt-out links scrolls past while he says the results were terrifying.
Prompt 2 typed: write the removal request for each site.
The plus menu opens with a red box drawn around the + button: 'here's the trick', turn on agent mode.
Agent browser window appears and visits a broker site on its own.
Prompt 4 result: a weekly scheduled removal task is created.
Cut back to his face for the keyword comment CTA, new title pill 'Comment Erase and I'll send you the prompts'.

why_it_works: Result shown before the method: the ticked list of broker removals at 3.6 s proves the claim, so the viewer stays to learn how.
Numbered prompts (1 to 4) give a clear progress structure, and 'here's the trick' / 'here's the best part' re-hook before the two strongest steps.
Fear of exposed personal data plus a do-nothing payoff ('while I just sit there') is a high-stakes, low-effort promise.
Keyword comment CTA ('comment Erase') trades the full prompts for comments, which explains the 2.5k comments and 26k shares.
weaknesses: Screen recording runs one 28.5 s shot with tiny UI text (median text height 2.2% of frame) that is hard to read on a phone.
Face appears only 14% of the time, so the personal presence from the hook disappears for most of the video.
Most text sits outside the safe area (83%), so UI overlays clash with TikTok's buttons.
for_robert: Copy the structure: show the finished result in the first cut, then walk through numbered prompts, and end with a keyword comment CTA. Fred could hold up the 'result' card at the cut, but keep the screen text big instead of a raw UI recording.
